messages.subject: Fwd: Re: BreedR remlf90 weights
parts:
Dear list,

As you can see from the discussion below (posted with permission), I
have introduced a new argument `weights` into `remlf90()` in order to
allow for a simple approach to heterogeneous variances.

See the vignette online or in the package for a demonstration of the
feature and more details.


Best wishes, and happy new year!

ƒacu.-

<mailto:facund...@inra.fr>>:

Stefano,

I see now how this is useful. It was something I had in my TODO list but
hadn't find the need for it so far.

It was not difficult to implement, so I did it and it is available from
breedR v11.5 which is already available in GitHub (i.e. if you install
with `devtools::install_github('famuvie/breedR')`.

In a few minutes it will also be available from the breedR's repository.
Thus, if you have set it up with the instructions at
http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/ <http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/>,
you will be able to just
`update.packages(oldPkgs = "breedR")`.

I also wrote a simple vignette with an explanation and a demonstration
of the model and the new feature (see
https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Heterogeneous-variances.pdf
<https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Heterogeneous-variances.pdf>).

Hope it helps.

ƒacu.-

P.S. Perhaps your "unexpected results" from using the WEIGHTS parameter
in airemlf90 were due to the fact that the weights bear an inverse
relationship with the residual variance. It was unintuitive for me: I
would have expected a direct one. See the vignette for more details, and
let me know whether it worked for you.
